grader.scenario: Broadband speed guarantee credit claim after sync speed remained below 45 Mbps minimum
grader.notes: Poor customer service call marked by agent rudeness, deflection of contractual ownership, failure of empathy, and repeated questioning, despite port reset temporarily resolving speed.

items.name: Branding and Survey Check
items.evidence: Agent opened with 'Thank you for calling S-Net broadband cancellations and billing' at [00:00] and closed with 'Thank you for choosing S-Net' in final lines.

items.name: Hold time and Dead Air
items.evidence: Holds announced with bear with me and thanked upon return without unmanaged dead air.

items.name: Verified customer
items.evidence: Verified full postal address and security PIN within the first 240 seconds.

items.name: Personalized the call/ticket appropriately
items.evidence: Agent addressed customer as Elena throughout the call.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: Customer expressed acute distress over missed architectural deadlines; agent offered no empathy.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: Agent never restated the customer's speed guarantee dispute in his own words.

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: Agent asked for router model at turn 26 despite customer providing Hub 4 serial number at turn 3.

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: Agent refused to book an engineer or raise claim, telling customer frontline staff do not handle disputes.

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: Agent insulted customer at [04:20]: 'Well if you had actually bothered to read section 8... don't accuse customer service of misleading you.'

items.name: Probing
items.evidence: Agent asked relevant diagnostic questions about speed test methods and test frequency.

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: Customer confirmed download speed reached 46.2 Mbps following DSLAM port reset and accepted ticket reference.
